findings.title: Unsafe access to metadata['sender']['login'] can cause a 500
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch compares the OAuth-authenticated user to integration.metadata['sender']['login']. Many legitimate Integration rows may not have metadata.sender (for example, integrations created before this change, installations where the webhook has not populated sender, or first-pass installations as shown in the tests). In those cases this direct subscripting can raise KeyError or TypeError and return a 500 instead of the intended graceful error page. The code should use safe lookups and fail closed when sender login is missing.

findings.title: User mismatch validation is skipped when the Integration row does not exist
findings.body: The new security check only runs after an Integration row exists. When Integration.DoesNotExist is raised, the view returns pipeline.next_step() without verifying that github_authenticated_user matches the installer. If the installation webhook that records sender is delayed, fails, or has not created/updated the Integration yet, the advertised mismatch validation is bypassed and an installation_id could potentially be completed by a different authenticated GitHub user. The flow should fail closed or otherwise verify installer identity before creating the integration.

findings.title: Query-string installation_id can override the pipeline-bound installation_id
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch uses request.GET.get('installation_id', pipeline.fetch_state('installation_id')), which lets a query-string parameter overwrite any installation_id already stored during the OAuth step. This weakens the binding between the GitHub OAuth identity and the installation ID. If an installation_id has already been bound in pipeline state, the view should use that value or require the query parameter to match it rather than silently allowing it to be swapped.

findings.title: OAuth token exchange omits redirect_uri
findings.body: The authorization request includes redirect_uri, but the access-token exchange sends only code, client_id, and client_secret. Omitting redirect_uri prevents Sentry from explicitly binding the code exchange to the callback URL used in the authorize step. This matters if the GitHub OAuth app can have multiple callback URLs or if a code could be obtained through another registered redirect URI. The same redirect_uri should be included in the token exchange.

findings.title: OAuth exchange and user-info fetch can raise 500 instead of showing the intended error
findings.body: safe_urlopen and get_user_info are called without exception handling; only parsing the response body is wrapped. Network timeouts, connection errors, HTTP errors, or exceptions raised by get_user_info will bubble up and produce a 500 instead of the intended installation-failed error page. The token exchange and user-info fetch should be wrapped and return error() on failure. Also treat an empty access_token as missing, not merely absent.

findings.title: Authorize redirect URL is built without URL encoding
findings.body: The GitHub authorize URL is constructed with an f-string, interpolating client_id, state, and redirect_uri directly into the query string. redirect_uri should be URL-encoded to avoid malformed or rejected URLs when reserved characters are present, and to make the construction robust to future changes. Use urllib.parse.urlencode to build the query parameters.

findings.title: Redirect can be built with installation_id=None
findings.body: If GitHub redirects with setup_action=install but without an installation_id, installation_id is None and is passed directly to reverse('integration-installation', args=[provider_id, installation_id]). This can generate a URL containing the literal None or cause a reverse/404 failure. The view should handle a missing installation_id with a graceful redirect or error page.
